name: Google Cloud Firestore
tagline: Serverless document database with realtime listeners, offline SDKs and a new Enterprise edition.
description: Firestore is Google Cloud's serverless document database, also sold as part of Firebase. It stores documents in collections and subcollections, runs on Spanner-class infrastructure with strongly consistent multi-region replication, and gives mobile and web clients realtime listeners, offline caching and security rules. The Enterprise edition, generally available in 2026, adds a MongoDB-compatible mode and a Pipeline query interface with joins, plus text and geospatial search (GA October 2026). Standard Firestore still requires an index for every query shape. It is the default for Firebase-style apps that want zero ops and pay-per-operation pricing.

pricing.startingPrice: Free quota: 1 GiB storage, 50k reads and 20k writes per day
pricing.notes: Standard edition bills per document read/write/delete; Enterprise edition bills by read/write units. Storage billed per GiB.

scale.notes: Automatic splitting; multi-region locations replicate writes synchronously. Sustained hot-spot writes to one document are limited to about 1 per second.

strengths: Truly serverless: no capacity planning, scales to zero cost at idle
Realtime listeners and offline persistence in the Firebase SDKs
Security Rules let clients talk to the database directly
Strongly consistent, ACID transactions even in multi-region mode
Enterprise edition adds MongoDB compatibility, joins and text search
Point-in-time recovery and reads at a past timestamp
weaknesses: Per-operation billing can explode with chatty listeners or fan-out reads
Standard edition has limited query expressiveness and needs composite indexes for most filters
Write rate limits on individual documents and on sequential keys
GCP-only, with proprietary APIs outside the Enterprise MongoDB mode
useCases: Mobile and web apps built on Firebase
User profiles and app state with offline support
Serverless backends on Cloud Run or Cloud Functions
notIdealFor: High-frequency counters or hot single documents
